explanations.answer: Raiders had killed all the older sons
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. Verse 1 says “the raiders who had come into the camp with the Arabs had killed all the older sons,” so the people of Jerusalem made Ahaziah king (2 Chronicles 22:1). I think this one hurts, so I won’t rush past it. That’s how the youngest ends up on the throne.

explanations.answer: The older sons turned down the throne
explanations.explanation: The text doesn’t have the older sons turning anything down. It says the raiders who had come into the camp with the Arabs had killed all the older sons (2 Chronicles 22:1). That’s a heavy detail, and I’d rather say it plainly. So the people of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, the youngest, king in his place.

explanations.answer: The older sons were away at war
explanations.explanation: Verse 1 doesn’t send the older sons off to war. It says the raiders who had come into the camp with the Arabs had killed all of them (2 Chronicles 22:1). That’s a heavy way for the story to start. Ahaziah, the youngest, is the one the people of Jerusalem made king.

Mother it is. The verse says “his mother was his counselor in wickedness” (2 Chronicles 22:3), and verse 2 gives her name, Athaliah (2 Chronicles 22:2). Everybody has a voice in their ear. His was the one the text calls his counselor in wickedness.

The passage doesn’t bring a wife into it. Verse 3 says “his mother was his counselor in wickedness” (2 Chronicles 22:3), and her name is Athaliah (2 Chronicles 22:2). Hunting for a wife in these verses is like opening a cookie box and finding only crumbs.

No sister shows up in these verses, friend, and nobody’s sister gets a speaking part. The counselor the text names is his mother: “his mother was his counselor in wickedness” (2 Chronicles 22:3). Her name is Athaliah, the granddaughter of Omri (2 Chronicles 22:2).

Destruction is what the verse says: “for to his destruction they were his counselors after the death of his father” (2 Chronicles 22:4). The house of Ahab became his counselors. You know when the GPS cheerfully sends you down a road that ends in a lake? Same idea, except Ahaziah’s road ran much longer.

Success would be a nice ending, but verse 4 says the counsel went the other direction. They were his counselors “to his destruction” after the death of his father (2 Chronicles 22:4). Advice that ends in destruction isn’t really advice. It’s a trapdoor with a friendly voice.

Honor sounds lovely, but it’s not what the verse says. The house of Ahab counseled Ahaziah “to his destruction” after the death of his father (2 Chronicles 22:4). Whatever those counselors promised, the text tells us where the counsel led.

Hazael king of Aram, baker. Verse 5 says Ahaziah went with Joram “to fight against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead” (2 Chronicles 22:5). Two kings go in together, and one king stands across from them. The text makes it easy to keep score.
This passage never mentions Mesha. The king on the other side in verse 5 is Hazael king of Aram (2 Chronicles 22:5). It’s the Arameans who wound Joram there.

Sennacherib doesn’t appear anywhere in these verses. Ahaziah goes with Joram “to fight against Hazael king of Aram” (2 Chronicles 22:5). Grabbing a king off the shelf at random is a bold strategy, but the text names the one.
True. Verse 5 says, “But the Arameans wounded Joram” (2 Chronicles 22:5). Joram son of Ahab is the one hurt in that fight. The wound count is right there in the verse.

The text says it did happen: “But the Arameans wounded Joram” (2 Chronicles 22:5). So the Arameans are the ones doing the wounding, and Joram son of Ahab is the one hurt. The verse doesn’t say Ahaziah was wounded there. It’s plain once you see it.

explanations.answer: Goes down to Jezreel to visit him
explanations.explanation: Right, he goes himself. Verse 6 says “Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to Jezreel to visit Joram son of Ahab, because Joram had been wounded” (2 Chronicles 22:6). Showing up in person with a box of cookies beats a text message any day. That’s a king making the trip.

explanations.answer: Sends a letter wishing him well
explanations.explanation: There’s no letter in verse 6. Ahaziah “went down to Jezreel to visit Joram son of Ahab” (2 Chronicles 22:6), and the text says it was because Joram had been wounded. Sending a note is a text-message move, and this king showed up in person.

Jerusalem is where Ahaziah reigned (2 Chronicles 22:2), but verse 6 sends him a different way. He “went down to Jezreel to visit Joram son of Ahab, because Joram had been wounded” (2 Chronicles 22:6). So he heads toward Joram instead of toward home.

God. Verse 7 says, “Ahaziah’s downfall came from God when he went to visit Joram” (2 Chronicles 22:7). That’s the text’s own statement, so I’ll let it stand just as it is. A visit that looks friendly, with a bigger story behind it.

Hazael is the king Ahaziah and Joram went to fight (2 Chronicles 22:5), but verse 7 doesn’t put the downfall on him. It says it came “from God when he went to visit Joram” (2 Chronicles 22:7). Hazael already had his moment back in verse 5.
Elijah doesn’t appear anywhere in these nine verses. Verse 7 says, “Ahaziah’s downfall came from God when he went to visit Joram” (2 Chronicles 22:7). The text names its source, and it isn’t Elijah.

Yes, baker. Verse 7 calls Jehu the one “whom the LORD had anointed to destroy the house of Ahab” (2 Chronicles 22:7). So Ahaziah and Joram go out to meet a man the LORD had anointed for exactly that job. The job is spelled out in the verse, plain as a label on a cookie box.

Peace with Judah isn’t in the verse. It says the LORD had anointed Jehu “to destroy the house of Ahab” (2 Chronicles 22:7). That’s the man Ahaziah and Joram go out to meet. The verse gives his job, and peace isn’t on the list.

Verse 7 doesn’t give Jehu a building job. It says the LORD had anointed him “to destroy the house of Ahab” (2 Chronicles 22:7). Samaria does show up in verse 9, as the place Ahaziah was hiding when he was captured (2 Chronicles 22:9). There’s nothing about walls anywhere.

Rulers. Verse 8 says Jehu “found the rulers of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah’s brothers who were serving Ahaziah, and he killed them” (2 Chronicles 22:8). This happened while Jehu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab. I think this one hurts, and I’d rather say so than hurry past it.

Verse 8 doesn’t name priests. It says Jehu found “the rulers of Judah” along with the sons of Ahaziah’s brothers who were serving Ahaziah, and he killed them (2 Chronicles 22:8). This is a heavy verse, so I’ll keep my words plain. The word the text uses is rulers.

Prophets aren’t mentioned in verse 8. The text says Jehu found “the rulers of Judah” and the sons of Ahaziah’s brothers who were serving Ahaziah (2 Chronicles 22:8). It’s a heavy verse, and I don’t want to dress it up. The word is rulers.

True. Verse 9 says Jehu looked for Ahaziah, and “Jehu’s soldiers captured him while he was hiding in Samaria” (2 Chronicles 22:9). So Jehu went looking, and his soldiers found him. After that, Ahaziah was brought to Jehu.

The text says it did happen. Verse 9 says “Jehu’s soldiers captured him while he was hiding in Samaria” (2 Chronicles 22:9). Jehu had gone looking for Ahaziah first. After the capture, Ahaziah was brought to Jehu.

explanations.answer: His grandfather Jehoshaphat sought the LORD
explanations.explanation: That’s the one, friend. They buried him, “for they said, ‘He is the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart’” (2 Chronicles 22:9). The reason in the text is their words about his grandfather. I think it’s striking that a grandfather’s heart still counted for something in that moment.

explanations.answer: He had been the king of Judah
explanations.explanation: The text doesn’t give his kingship as the reason. It gives what they said: “He is the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart” (2 Chronicles 22:9). Ahaziah did reign in Jerusalem for one year (2 Chronicles 22:2), but the burial reason points back to his grandfather.

explanations.answer: His mother Athaliah asked them to
explanations.explanation: Verse 9 never says Athaliah asked for anything. Her name appears in verse 2 as Ahaziah’s mother (2 Chronicles 22:2). The reason for the burial is what they said: “He is the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart” (2 Chronicles 22:9).

The verse says the opposite, friend. It ends, “So no one was left from the house of Ahaziah with the strength to rule the kingdom” (2 Chronicles 22:9). Jehu had already killed the sons of Ahaziah’s brothers who were serving him (2 Chronicles 22:8). So the statement doesn’t match what the text says.

You got it, baker. The verse ends, “So no one was left from the house of Ahaziah with the strength to rule the kingdom” (2 Chronicles 22:9). Before that, Jehu had killed the sons of Ahaziah’s brothers who were serving him (2 Chronicles 22:8). That’s a heavy end to the passage. No one in his house was left with the strength to rule.
